children: rose 12.10% intraday, as of 10:00 a.m. ET, after the cruise operator reported record third-quarter revenue of $8.44 billion and net income of $1.92 billion, or $1.40 a diluted share, up from $1.33 a year earlier. Adjusted EPS, a non-GAAP measure, was $1.43, flat with last year despite a $0.10 hit from higher fuel prices and currency moves.

Results came in ahead of Carnival's own June guidance. Net yields rose 2.4% in constant currency, more than a point better than guided, and adjusted EBITDA of $3.0 billion matched last year's record and beat guidance by $110 million.

Third-quarter customer deposits reached a record $7.6 billion, up $0.5 billion from a year earlier despite flat capacity, and booked occupancy and pricing for 2027 are at record levels. CEO Josh Weinstein said the booking curve "reinforces our confidence in the durability of demand." Carnival has bought back about $1.2 billion of stock this year and won an investment-grade rating from S&P during the quarter.

For the full year, Carnival expects adjusted net income of about $3.08 billion, or $2.24 a share, with more than $150 million of operational improvement versus June offsetting a similar hit from higher fuel costs.

title: Carnival Stock Rises 12% as Record Deposits Signal Strong 2027
